Resolves #18954

Arrow navigation now resolves the grid's open edit before its selection model moves. A valid suspended draft commits once and retires its editor; an invalid draft keeps its selection and brings the same editor back into view with its error visible. A shared `BaseModel#canNavigate` admission calls CellEditing's terminal before the existing CellModel/RowModel/ColumnModel handlers. Cell-selecting models anchor the arrow at the edited cell after committing, including when double-click activation left nothing selected. Invalid Tab and arrows reuse one reveal/focus method; field and picker keys retain their current path. The Grids guide describes the behavior.

Related: #18762. [GPT epic return evaluation](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18762#issuecomment-5741956596).

Evidence: L2 (real keys in headed Chromium, App Worker state and event order, rendered focus/validation) → L2 required (the suspended edit terminal and selection behavior). Residual: none.

The branch includes the merged RowModel and deferred-render fixes (#18943, #18955); Tab now uses their `editInSight` helper, and obsolete index variables were removed.

The pre-existing drag-test flake recorded in #18955 was fixed independently by #18960, now included in this branch's base.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — two findings, both measured at `412ccfebd8`** (a scratch e2e probe on the pooled fixture, deleted afterwards).

**F1 — an arrow commit leaves no anchor, so navigation starts from nowhere.** Under `CellModel`, a double-click opens the edit with the selection empty (the second click toggles the cell off; Vega measured it for #18961). Probe: double-click `r3c3`, fill a valid draft, scroll to 4000, ArrowDown on the View.

| head | worker log | selected afterwards | View |
|---|---|---|---|
| `412ccfebd8` | `commit:c3`, `select` | `r2c0` | scrolled to the top |
| + repair below | `commit:c3`, `select`… | `r4c3` | follows `r4` |

The commit is right. The navigation then runs from an empty selection, and the user who was editing r3 lands on r2's first column. `onEnterKey` closed this exact gap for its own commit (#18912): *"a commit that ends the edit in place leaves the cell selected, so the arrow keys have an anchor"*. The arrow terminal is a commit that ends the edit too, and needs the anchor more, because its navigation runs immediately. Your arms don't see it: every cell-model arm activates by click then Enter, which keeps the cell selected — the ticket chose that on purpose to avoid the toggle confound, but the confound is the case users hit.

Repair, run at your head — the PR's 28 arrow arms stay green with it:

```js
onNavigationKey(data) {
    let me        = this,
        {session} = me;

    if (!session || data.path?.[0]?.id !== me.owner.view.id) {
        return true
    }

    // Read before the commit ends the session
    let {view}           = me.owner,
        {selectionModel} = view,
        {dataField}      = session,
        record           = me.getRecord(session);

    if (me.completeEdit()) {
        // The edited cell is the anchor the arrow moves from, as after Enter
        record && selectionModel?.selectsCells && selectionModel.select(view.getLogicalCellId(record, dataField));
        return true
    }

    me.focusEdit(session);
    return false
}
```

Row-selecting models need nothing: #18941's `startEdit` already selects the row, which is why your double-click-activated row arms pass.

**F2 — `ColumnModel`'s arrows bypass the gate.** `selection.grid.ColumnModel#onKeyDownLeft` and `#onKeyDownRight` still read `!this.hasEditorFocus(data) && …`. Probe under `ColumnModel` (loaded and set on the View the way your arms set the combined models): double-click `r3c3`, valid draft, scroll to 4000, ArrowRight → the editor is still alive, the worker log is empty, and scrolling back shows the open editor with its draft. The Contract Ledger row — *"View arrows during a suspended edit: resolve a valid edit before existing model navigation"* — names no model. Routing both handlers through `canNavigate(data)`, as you did for `CellModel` and `RowModel`, closes it. AC-3 names cell- and row-selecting models only; the gate you added is shared precisely so that no arrow consumer is left outside it.

Cleared, looked for: a second commit after a successful terminal (your log arms pin exactly one); the veto leaving the selection moved (pinned); focus in a mounted editor or picker losing its own arrows (your added mounted-input keys, and `hasEditorFocus` short-circuits first); `onNavigationKey` firing for a key whose first path node is not the View (guarded); `focusEdit()`'s column index matching the old `columnIndex` (`owner.columns.indexOf` is the same index space); and #18938's `refocus` rule composing with the veto — the veto moves no selection, so the owed refocus survives, and a second `focus()` from `focusEdit`'s mounted listener is harmless.
